content: When co-administering oral microbiota products with antibiotics, it is critical to consider the pharmacodynamic interactions that may occur. Antibiotics such as vancomycin, amikacin, amoxicillin, ampicillin, azithromycin, aztreonam, bacitracin, cefaclor, cefadroxil, cefazolin, cefdinir, cefditoren, cefepime, cefepime/enmetazobactam, cefiderocol, cefixime, cefotaxime, cefotetan, cefoxitin, cefpirome, cefpodoxime, cefprozil, ceftaroline, ceftazidime, ceftazidime/avibactam, ceftibuten, ceftizoxime, ceftolozane/tazobactam, ceftriaxone, cefuroxime, cephalexin, chloramphenicol, ciprofloxacin, clindamycin, colistin, dalbavancin, daptomycin, delafloxacin, demeclocycline, dicloxacillin, doxycycline, eravacycline, ertapenem, erythromycin base, erythromycin ethylsuccinate, and erythromycin lactobionate can reduce the efficacy of oral microbiota products. This reduction in efficacy is due to pharmacodynamic antagonism, as these antibiotics may inhibit the activity or survival of bacterial spores contained in the oral microbiota products. To mitigate this interaction, it is recommended to complete the full course of antibiotics 2 to 4 days prior to initiating oral microbiota therapy. This allows for the clearance of the antibiotic from the system, reducing its inhibitory effects on the microbiota. If the use of these antibiotics is unavoidable, alternative therapeutic options should be considered to preserve the efficacy of the oral microbiota product.
